date_note: Abnormal access first detected about 9:30 a.m. Friday 13 Nov (KST), the date used; the article, published 16 Nov, gives the weekday, not the calendar date. Cause stated in a second statement on Monday 16 Nov.
title: Korea Minting Corp. says outsider exploited API flaw in 'Chak' local-currency platform, data of 3,083 customers leaked
org: Korea Minting and Security Printing Corp.
summary: The Herald Business reports that Korea Minting and Security Printing Corp. detected abnormal access to its Chak platform around 9:30 a.m. on 13 November, blocked suspect IPs including overseas ones and shut the system. A second statement said an outsider exploited an authentication flaw in an API used to exchange data between systems. Texts went to all 3,083 affected customers; the corporation says its other voucher and ID systems are physically separate.
plain: A South Korean state mint's local-currency app was accessed by an outsider and data on 3,083 customers leaked.
exec: A flaw in an API let an outsider reach customer data at a state body; API authentication is a common weak point.
action: Review authentication on APIs that exchange data between systems; Chak users should ignore unexpected texts or calls asking for money or codes.
